3. The case of the present petitioner as plaintiff, in brief, is that on 03.12.1974 she had purchased her said land from one Kasiruddin and within year she constructed thereon a one storied building. Subsequently one Shahidul Islam pahloan and others filed a partition suit in the court of the learned Subordinate Judge. It was numbered 398 of 2001. She was impleaded in it as the defendant No.9. On 06.04.1983 a preliminary decree was passed. Following it a survey was conducted it was then found that the land on which she had her building constructed fell in the saham of Shahidul Islam. So to keep the building and the land on which it is standing in her possession by a deed of exchange dated 27.10.1984 she exchanged her 6 decimals land with 7.5 decimals land of Shahidul Islam pahloan. On 01.12.1984 the present respondent purchased 3 decimals of land to the east of her land. In 1987 he started construction on it, encroaching upon her land. She raised objection, but he paid no need. So she approached Jamalpur pourashava. The pourashava by their memo No. 2694 dated 02.08.1987 asked the present respondent not to carry on with his construction, but of no avail. The present petitioner taking periodic advantage of her absence from her land completed his construction, encroaching upon her land. On 03.06.1988 a salish was effected between the parties under the auspices of the pourashava. It was decided in the said salish that the present respondent would demolish his house within a year and construct a new one with a plan approved by the pourashava leaving 3 feet vacant to the west of his house. He moved his boundary to the east by 6 link. However, he did not demolish his house. So she asked him on 03.11.1989 to break his house and take 3 feet back inside his compound, to which he paid no heed. So she filed her suit for a mandatory injunction requiring the present respondent to break his house and take it back by 3 feet inside his compound. 

 5. The learned Additional Assistant Judge dismissed the other class Suit No. 53 of 1991 instituted by the present petitioner, but decreed the other Class Suit No. 55 of 1991 filed by the respondent by the judgment decree dated 21.04.1992. 

 6. The present petitioner filed two appeals before the learned District Judge against the judgment and decree passed in the aforesaid other class suite i.e. other Class Suit No. 53 of 1991 (filed by the present petitioner) and other Class Suit No.55 of 1991 (filed by the present respondent). The appeals were ultimately heard by the teamed subordinate Judge (at present Joint District Judge) and Artha Rin Adalat, Jamalpur. 

 7. Against the judgment and decree dated 21.04.1992 passed in other Class Suit No. 53 of 1991 the present petitioner filed other Class Appeal No.35 of 1992 and against the judgment and decree dated 21.04.1992 passed in other Class Suit No.55 of 1991 the present petitioner filed other Class Appeal No. 36 of 1992. The learned Subordinate Judge allowed both the appeals. The learned Subordinate Judge dismissed other Class Suit No.55 of 1991 and decreed the Other Class Suit No. 53 of 1991. 

 8. The present respondent filed two civil revisions before the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1214 of 1994 was filed against the judgment and decree passed in Other Class Appeal No. 35 of 1992 (which arose in respect of judgment and decree passed Other Class Suit No. 53 of 1991). Civil Revision No. 1213 of 1994 was filed against the judgment and decree passed in Other Class Appeal No. 36 of 1992 (which arose in respect of judgment and decree passed Other Class Suit No.55 of 1991).
